history.period: c. 1025–1050 CE (reign of Vidyadhara, r. c. 1003–1035)
history.summary: The Kandariya Mahadeva is the largest and most ornate temple of the Western Group at Khajuraho, and the pinnacle of Chandela Nagara architecture. It was commissioned by King Vidyadhara, whose name appears (as 'Virimda') in an inscription on a mandapa pilaster, to celebrate his victory over Mahmud of Ghazni; its towering 84-spired shikhara symbolises Mount Kailash. The sandstone temple stands ~31 m tall and is adorned with around 870–900 sculptures of gods, celestial beings and scenes of daily life, including erotic art. Inscribed with the Khajuraho Group of Monuments on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1986; maintained by the ASI. NOTE: popular quiz sources date it to 999 CE under Dhangadeva — scholarly consensus is Vidyadhara, 1025–1050 CE (verify). name: Kandariya Mahadev Temple
town_description: Khajuraho is a small town in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh, world-famous for its group of 9th–11th century Hindu and Jain temples built by the Chandela dynasty. The temple complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, drawing visitors for its Nagara architecture and intricate sculpture. The town is a compact tourist hub with hotels, the Khajuraho Dance Festival grounds, and an ASI archaeological museum.

travel.road: Western Group, ~1 km from Khajuraho bus stand; town is on NH 39

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Khajuraho Dance Festival (Feb–Mar)
